reason: Start tracing glucose across the intestinal lining toward the liver.
expectation: Glucose should enter the villus and reach its blood vessels, though further steps may be needed to reach the liver.

reaction: The result matches my expectation, though it doesn't explain the transport mechanism.
reason: Trace amino acids across the same boundary to advance the first goal.
expectation: Amino acids will enter a villus blood capillary, with a further step possibly needed to reach the liver.

alternatives.reason: Fat absorption is also a goal, but finishing the blood-borne nutrients first seems straightforward.

effect: Both glucose and amino acids have reached villus blood; combining them may advance their route to the liver.
reaction: The parallel result is clear but repetitive, and the transport mechanism remains unexplained.
reason: Continue the blood-borne nutrient route toward the liver.
expectation: The two nutrients will be shown travelling together in blood, possibly toward the liver.

alternatives.reason: Fat absorption is also required, but I want to advance the current route first.

effect: The glucose and amino acid route to the liver is complete; I can now focus on fat absorption.
reaction: The portal-blood result clearly connects the two nutrient paths to the liver.
reason: Start tracing fat digestion products across the villus.
expectation: Fat digestion products will enter intestinal cells, probably before packaging and lymph entry.

alternatives.reason: Packaging materials will likely be needed, but I want to follow the fat into the villus first.

effect: Fatty acids and monoglycerides are inside the intestinal cells, ready for the packaging step.
reaction: The result matches my expectation, though it does not explain how they crossed the cell boundary.
reason: Package the absorbed fat before sending it into lymph.
expectation: The cell will assemble the fat products into lipoprotein particles, with another step needed for lymph entry.

alternatives.reason: The lacteal entrance will be needed for lymph entry, but packaging seems the next step.

effect: The fat products have been rebuilt and packaged into chylomicrons, ready for the lymph route.
reaction: The explanation clarifies what the packaging step accomplishes, although the particle's name is new.
reason: Use the lacteal entrance to send the packaged fat into lymph.
expectation: Chylomicrons will enter the villus lymph vessel, completing the fat-transport goal.

effect: The chylomicrons entered the villus lymph vessel, completing the fat route; lymph carries them onward to blood.
reaction: The final result clearly contrasts fat’s route with the portal-blood route.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following fat into cells, packaging it as chylomicrons, and sending it into lymph made the different nutrient routes concrete. The planned pictures and brief explanations connect the steps well.

leastWorthwhile.text: The separate glucose and amino-acid crossings felt repetitive. Their planned pictures show where the molecules go but do not explain how they cross the intestinal cells.

surprise.text: The explanation that intestinal cells rebuild fat before packaging it clarified what chylomicrons are, though the name was new to me.

arbitrary.text: Combining glucose and amino acids already in villus blood felt somewhat mechanical, though the resulting shared route toward the liver had a clear purpose.

continue.text: I would probably continue: comparing the blood and lymph routes was useful, though I would hope for more explanation of transport mechanisms and less repetitive setup.
